## Purpose

This SOP describes the determination of five-day biochemical oxygen
demand (BOD~5~) in water and wastewater samples using the manometric
method (WTW OxiTop system). BOD~5~ is a measure of the dissolved
oxygen consumed by microorganisms during the aerobic decomposition of
organic matter over a five-day incubation period at 20 °C and is the
standard regulatory indicator of organic pollution load in water
[@apha2012; @usepa405_1].


## Scope

- **Applies to:** Surface water, wastewater, and effluent samples
  analyzed for BOD~5~ using the WTW OxiTop manometric method in the
  EA Program laboratory
- **Does not apply to:** Carbonaceous BOD (CBOD) with nitrification
  inhibitor; BOD by Winkler titration or dissolved oxygen probe
  methods; chemical oxygen demand (COD)
- **Location:** Biogeochemistry Laboratory, Pomona College


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                                          |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------|
| PI / Lab Manager  | Approve SOP; review QC data; maintain equipment         |
| Trained Personnel | Prepare reagents, run analyses, record results          |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent use                |


## Definitions

- **Biochemical oxygen demand (BOD):** The mass of dissolved oxygen
  consumed per unit volume of sample by microbial oxidation of organic
  matter under aerobic conditions at 20 °C; expressed in mg/L
  [@apha2012].
- **BOD~5~:** BOD measured over a 5-day incubation period at 20 °C;
  the standard regulatory measure of organic pollution load in surface
  water and effluent [@apha2012; @usepa405_1].
- **Carbonaceous BOD (CBOD):** BOD attributable to carbon-containing
  organic compounds; measured in the presence of a nitrification
  inhibitor (allylthiourea) to prevent oxygen consumption by nitrifying
  bacteria from contributing to the result.
- **Dilution water:** Aerated, buffered, nutrient-supplemented
  deionized water used to dilute concentrated samples to bring the
  expected BOD~5~ into the measurable range of the OxiTop system
  [@apha2012].
- **Glucose-glutamic acid (GGA) check standard:** A standard seed-check
  solution prepared at 150 mg/L glucose + 150 mg/L glutamic acid;
  expected BOD~5~ of 198 ±30.5 mg/L; used to verify seed quality and
  method performance [@apha2012, Method 5210 B].
- **Manometric method (OxiTop):** A closed-system BOD measurement
  technique in which O~2~ consumption is tracked by measuring the
  resulting decrease in headspace pressure; CO~2~ produced during
  microbial respiration is absorbed by NaOH pellets, ensuring that
  pressure changes reflect only oxygen consumption [@wtw_oxitop].
- **Nitrification:** Microbial oxidation of ammonia to nitrate by
  nitrifying bacteria; consumes dissolved oxygen and can inflate BOD
  values if not inhibited in carbonaceous BOD analyses.
- **Seeding:** Addition of a microbial inoculum (e.g., diluted
  wastewater or settled sewage) to dilution water to ensure adequate
  microbial activity when samples lack native microorganisms
  [@apha2012].


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Chemical:** Nutrient buffer solutions contain phosphate and
  ammonium salts; NaOH pellets (CO~2~ absorbent) are corrosive.
  Handle with gloves and avoid skin or eye contact.
- **Biological:** Wastewater samples may contain pathogens. Treat all
  samples as potentially infectious.
- **Physical:** Glass BOD bottles are fragile. Handle with care to
  avoid breakage.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Safety glasses or goggles
- [ ] Lab coat
- [ ] Nitrile gloves

### Emergency Procedures

In case of chemical spill or exposure, refer to
[SOP-L004 Chemical Spill Response](SOP-L004-chemical-spill-response.qmd)
or call Campus Safety. For NaOH contact with skin or eyes, flush
immediately with copious water for at least 15 minutes and seek
medical attention.


## Equipment and Materials

### Equipment

| Item                                      | Notes                             |
|:------------------------------------------|:----------------------------------|
| WTW OxiTop manometers (≥ 3 per run)       | One blank + two samples minimum; check battery [@wtw_oxitop] |
| BOD~5~ incubation bottles (nominal 500 mL) | Brown glass with neck adapter    |
| Rubber quivers (CO~2~ absorber holders)   | One per bottle                    |
| Incubator at 20.0 ±1.0 °C                | Verify temperature daily          |
| Magnetic stirrer platform (in incubator)  | Low-speed continuous stirring     |
| Magnetic stir bars                        | One per bottle                    |
| 500 mL graduated cylinder                 |                                   |
| Micropipette, 100--1000 µL                | With disposable tips              |
| pH meter                                  | Calibrated per [SOP-L300](SOP-L300-pH-conductivity-bench.qmd) |
| Air pump with diffuser stone              | For aerating dilution water       |

### Consumables

| Item                    | Storage       | Notes                              |
|:------------------------|:--------------|:-----------------------------------|
| NaOH pellets            | Desiccator    | CO~2~ absorbent; 2 pellets per bottle |
| Phosphate buffer stock  | Refrigerator  | See §6                             |
| MgSO~4~, CaCl~2~, FeCl~3~ solutions | Shelf | See §6                        |
| Seed inoculum (if needed) | Fresh       | Settled domestic wastewater or commercial seed |


## Reagents and Dilution Water

### Nutrient Stock Solutions

Prepare the following four stock solutions; add 1 mL of each per liter
of dilution water [@apha2012]:

1. **Phosphate buffer:** Dissolve 8.5 g KH~2~PO~4~, 21.75 g K~2~HPO~4~,
   33.4 g Na~2~HPO~4~·7H~2~O, and 1.7 g NH~4~Cl in ~500 mL deionized
   water and dilute to 1 L (pH 7.2).
2. **Magnesium sulfate:** Dissolve 22.5 g MgSO~4~·7H~2~O in deionized
   water; dilute to 1 L.
3. **Calcium chloride:** Dissolve 27.5 g CaCl~2~ in deionized water;
   dilute to 1 L.
4. **Ferric chloride:** Dissolve 0.25 g FeCl~3~·6H~2~O in deionized
   water; dilute to 1 L.

### Dilution Water Preparation

1. Fill a clean 1 L vessel with deionized water.
2. Add 1 mL of each stock solution.
3. Aerate with an air pump for at least 1 hour to bring DO near
   saturation.
4. Verify pH is 6.8--7.2; adjust with dilute HCl or NaOH if necessary.
5. Allow to equilibrate to 20 °C before use.

### Measuring Range and Sample Volume Selection

| Expected BOD~5~ (mg/L) | Total volume (mL) | Sample (mL) | DI water (mL) |
|:-----------------------|:------------------|:------------|:--------------|
| 0--40                  | 432               | 216         | 216           |
| 0--80                  | 365               | 182.5       | 182.5         |
| 0--200                 | 250               | 125         | 125           |
| 0--400                 | 164               | 82          | 82            |
| 0--800                 | 97                | 48.5        | 48.5          |
| 0--2000                | 43.5              | 21.75       | 21.75         |

: Volume selection for WTW OxiTop BOD~5~ analysis based on expected concentration [@wtw_oxitop]. {#tbl-volumes}

For most EA Program surface water samples, the 0--200 mg/L range is a
reasonable starting point. If the expected concentration is unknown,
run samples at two dilutions.


## Procedure

### Preparation (Day 0)

1. Calibrate the pH meter per [SOP-L300](SOP-L300-pH-conductivity-bench.qmd).
2. Prepare dilution water as described above; make enough for all
   blanks and samples.
3. Allow refrigerated samples to equilibrate to 20 °C. Add seed
   inoculum to both sample and blank bottles if seeding is required.
4. Verify that all OxiTop manometers are functional (battery check,
   reset previous readings) [@wtw_oxitop].

### Bottle Setup

1. Place a clean magnetic stir bar in each BOD~5~ bottle.
2. Measure the appropriate sample volume into each sample bottle
   (see @tbl-volumes).
3. Add the corresponding volume of dilution water.
4. For the blank bottle, add dilution water only (same total volume as
   sample bottles).
5. Place 2 NaOH pellets in each rubber quiver. Insert the quiver into
   the bottle neck above the liquid surface.
6. Screw the OxiTop manometer head onto each bottle; ensure a
   gas-tight seal.

::: {.callout-tip}
### Labeling
Label each bottle (Blank, Sample A-1, Sample A-2, etc.) on both the
bottle and the manometer before starting incubation. Record bottle
assignments in the lab notebook.
:::

### Incubation

1. Place all bottles on the magnetic stirrer platform inside the
   incubator at 20.0 ±1.0 °C.
2. Activate the OxiTop manometers to begin recording pressure.
3. Incubate for five days (120 ±2 hours) in the dark; keep the
   incubator door closed except for daily temperature checks
   [@apha2012].
4. Verify incubator temperature at least once daily; record in the
   instrument logbook.

### Reading Results (Day 5)

1. Read the BOD~5~ value from each OxiTop manometer; the instrument
   converts pressure decrease to mg/L automatically based on the
   selected measuring range [@wtw_oxitop].
2. Record all readings in the lab notebook: setup and reading dates/
   times, incubator temperature log, measuring range, sample IDs, and
   replicate values.
3. Remove bottles from the incubator. Discard sample water per §9.
   Clean bottles and stir bars thoroughly with hot water and detergent;
   rinse with deionized water.


## Data Analysis and Calculations

### OxiTop Direct Reading

The OxiTop system calculates BOD~5~ internally from the headspace
pressure decrease [@wtw_oxitop]. Record the displayed mg/L value
directly.

### Blank Correction

$$
\text{BOD}_{5,\text{corrected}} = \text{BOD}_{5,\text{sample}} - \text{BOD}_{5,\text{blank}}
$$

The blank must be less than 0.2 mg/L for unseeded dilution water
[@apha2012]. If the blank exceeds 0.2 mg/L, investigate dilution water
quality and consider re-running the analysis.

### Dilution Factor

For highly concentrated samples diluted beyond the standard OxiTop
protocol:

$$
\text{BOD}_{5,\text{final}} = \text{BOD}_{5,\text{corrected}} \times \frac{V_{\text{total}}}{V_{\text{sample}}}
$$

For standard OxiTop runs, the dilution factor is already incorporated
into the displayed result.


## Quality Control

- Run at least one blank per analytical batch [@apha2012].
- Run duplicate sample bottles for each sample; RPD must be less than
  20%.
- If available, include a GGA check standard at 300 mg/L combined
  (150 mg/L each); expected BOD~5~ = 198 ±30.5 mg/L
  [@apha2012, Method 5210 B].
- Blank BOD~5~ must be less than 0.2 mg/L (unseeded) or less than
  0.6 mg/L (seeded) [@apha2012].
- Verify incubator temperature is 20.0 ±1.0 °C throughout incubation.
- Log all QC results; flag and consult the PI if criteria are not met.


## Troubleshooting

| Problem                        | Possible Cause                     | Corrective Action                |
|:-------------------------------|:-----------------------------------|:---------------------------------|
| No pressure change after 5 days | Dead battery; poor seal           | Check battery; reseat manometer  |
| Blank BOD~5~ too high          | Contaminated dilution water        | Reclean bottles; prepare fresh dilution water |
| Replicate RPD > 20%            | Heterogeneous sample               | Mix samples well; check pipette calibration |
| BOD~5~ exceeds range           | Sample more concentrated than expected | Re-run at higher range (lower volume) |
| Negative BOD~5~                | Leak in bottle seal; NaOH saturated | Inspect seal; use fresh NaOH pellets |


## Waste Disposal

| Waste Type              | Disposal Method                                |
|:------------------------|:-----------------------------------------------|
| Analyzed sample water   | Drain with copious water (if non-hazardous)    |
| NaOH pellets (used)     | Dissolve in water, neutralize, drain           |
| Dilution water          | Drain                                          |
| Broken glass            | Sharps container                               |

## Training Record

Before performing BOD~5~ analysis independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Complete [SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd)
   training
3. Review the WTW OxiTop operating manual [@wtw_oxitop]
4. Observe a trained operator perform the complete procedure (setup
   through Day 5 reading)
5. Perform the analysis under supervision with acceptable QC results
   (duplicate RPD within 20%; blank within criteria)
6. Be signed off by the PI or lab manager
